    Eradication feasibility

    Source: R/inv-biosecurity.R
    inv_eradication_feasibility.Rd

    Projects an incursion under repeated control with a simple stochastic removal model. Each year the population grows by exp(growth_rate) and is searched rounds times; each individual (or patch) is found with probability detect_prob per round and removed with probability efficacy once found. The annual multiplier is lambda = exp(growth_rate) * (1 - detect_prob * efficacy)^rounds, the expected population after t years is population * lambda^t, and the probability that no individual remains is exp(-population * lambda^t) (Poisson approximation). Eradication is feasible only when lambda < 1.

    Usage

    inv_eradication_feasibility(
  .data,
  population,
  growth_rate,
  detect_prob,
  efficacy = 1,
  rounds = 1,
  area = NULL,
  cost_per_unit = NULL,
  horizon = 10,
  target = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per incursion or scenario.

    population

    Initial number of individuals or patches.

    growth_rate

    Intrinsic annual growth rate r (log scale).

    detect_prob

    Probability of detecting an individual per search round.

    efficacy

    Probability that a detected individual is removed.

    rounds

    Search rounds per year.

    area

    Optional infested area (for example in hectares), used for cost.

    cost_per_unit

    Optional cost of one search round per unit area.

    horizon

    Planning horizon in years for p_eradicated.

    target

    Probability of eradication that defines success.

    Value

    .data as a tibble with added columns lambda, feasible, min_rounds (fewest rounds per year giving lambda < 1), years_to_target (years until the eradication probability reaches target, Inf when not feasible), p_eradicated (probability of eradication within horizon years) and, when cost is given, total_cost (cost of all rounds up to years_to_target).

    Details

    Every argument after .data uses data masking, so each can be a column of .data or a constant.

    References

    Regan, T. J., McCarthy, M. A., Baxter, P. W. J., Panetta, F. D. and Possingham, H. P. (2006). Optimal eradication: when to stop looking for an invasive plant. Ecology Letters, 9, 759-766. doi:10.1111/j.1461-0248.2006.00920.x

    Examples

    scenarios <- data.frame(
  site = c("small", "medium", "large"),
  n0 = c(20, 400, 15000),
  ha = c(2, 50, 900)
)
inv_eradication_feasibility(scenarios, population = n0, growth_rate = 0.4,
  detect_prob = 0.6, efficacy = 0.95, rounds = 2, area = ha,
  cost_per_unit = 120)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 9
#>   site      n0    ha lambda feasible min_rounds years_to_target p_eradicated
#>   <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <lgl>         <dbl>           <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 small     20     2  0.276 TRUE              1               5        1.000
#> 2 medium   400    50  0.276 TRUE              1               7        0.999
#> 3 large  15000   900  0.276 TRUE              1              10        0.962
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: total_cost <dbl>
